Sample matrix: Whole Blood (collected in "serum tubes" containing an inert polymeric serum separator gel and a clotting activation factor)
Preparation Procedure: - Centrifuge for 10-15 min at 1300-1500 g as soon as possible after reception. - Take a serum Aliquot of the "A" Sample to be used for the ITP. The remaining of the "A" Sample serum fraction not used for the ITP may be kept in the Sample collection tube or aliquoted into new vials, which shall be properly labelled to ensure Laboratory Chain of Custody (LCOC) documentation, and stored frozen until the "A" CP, if needed. - If the separated serum fraction is kept in the Sample collection tube, step- freeze it for storage according to the tube manufacturer's instructions until analysis, if needed<sup>+</sup> . - For the ITP, analyze ''A'' Sample Aliquots immediately after aliquoting or store them at approximately 4 °C for a maximum of 24 h before analysis (within a maximum of 4 days from Sample collection). Alternatively, keep the ''A'' Sample Aliquots frozen until analysis.

Sample matrix: Whole Blood (collected in "serum tubes" containing an inert polymeric serum separator gel and a clotting activation factor)
Preparation Procedure: - Centrifuge for 10-15 minutes at 1300-1500 g as soon as possible after reception. - Keep the whole of the "B" Sample separated serum fraction in the Sample collection tube and step-freeze according to the tube manufacturer's instructions until analysis, if needed<sup>+</sup> . - Once the "B" Sample is thawed and opened, keep the remaining serum fraction not used for the "B" CP in the Sample collection tube or transfer it into a new tube/vial. (Re)-seal it in front of the Athlete or the Athlete's representative or an Independent Witness, as applicable, using a tamper- evident system. Keep the Sample in frozen storage until Further Analysis, if needed.
